subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence.

She was feeling **under the weather**, so she decided to go to bed in order to sleep.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Hit the sack**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Under the weather"** means feeling unwell or slightly ill. (बीमार महसूस करना)

 
 
• **Example:** He has been feeling under the weather since yesterday, so he decided to rest at home.
 
 
 
• **"Hit the sack"** refers to going to bed to sleep. (सोने जाना)
 
 
• **Example:** After a long day at work, she was so tired that she decided to hit the sack early.
 
 
 
• In this context, the highlighted phrase "under the weather" suggests that she was not feeling well, so the correct idiom to describe her action of going to bed is "hit the sack."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Bark up the wrong tree** (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना): To pursue a mistaken or misguided course of action.

 
 
• **Example:** If you think I took your book, you're barking up the wrong tree.
 
 
 
• **Cry over spilled milk** (बीती बातों पर पछताना): To waste time worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be changed.
 
 
• **Example:** There's no use crying over spilled milk; we need to move on and find a solution.
 
 
 
• **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): A way of wishing someone good luck, especially before a performance.
 
 
• **Example:** You're going to do great in the play tonight! Break a leg!
